claim: Three open-source tools dominate GenAI evaluation in 2026: Promptfoo (security/red-teaming, YAML configs), DeepEval (30+ metrics, pytest-style), and RAGAS (RAG-specific retrieval/generation metrics).
quote: Three open-source tools dominate the GenAI evaluation landscape in 2026: Promptfoo, DeepEval, and RAGAS.

claim: DeepEval is an open-source framework offering 30+ metrics including G-Eval (LLM-as-judge) and deterministic options, designed for unit-testing LLM apps like pytest.
quote: DeepEval is an open-source evaluation framework offering over 30 distinct metrics, including advanced techniques like G-Eval (LLM-as-judge) and deterministic options.

claim: RAGAS metrics (faithfulness, context precision, context recall, answer relevancy) are purpose-built for retrieval-augmented generation and widely cited in research.
quote: Its metrics -- faithfulness, context precision, context recall, answer relevancy -- are specifically designed for retrieval-augmented generation and widely cited in research.

claim: Braintrust autoevals provides prebuilt model-graded scorers (e.g. Factuality) for Python and JS, many adapted from OpenAI's evals project, and defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY for the judge.
quote: Many of these evaluations are adapted from OpenAI's excellent evals project... By default, Autoevals uses your OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable to authenticate with OpenAI's API.

claim: Arize Phoenix supports both deterministic code-based evaluators and LLM-as-judge evaluators, is OTel-native/vendor-agnostic, and offers model-agnostic adapters to swap judge models across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, LiteLLM.
quote: Phoenix supports both deterministic code-based evaluators (exact match, regex, custom heuristics) and LLM-as-a-judge evaluators. Phoenix is vendor and language agnostic

claim: OpenAI Evals offers grader types: string_check (deterministic), text_similarity (cosine/bleu/rouge/etc returning a float vs pass_threshold), and score_model (LLM assigns numeric 0-1 score with reasoning); local graders are fastest.
quote: The score grader (score_model) uses an LLM to assign a numeric score to model outputs... String_check and text_similarity are generally the fastest graders as those are executed local to the training loop.

claim: OpenAI is deprecating its Evals platform: read-only for existing users on Oct 31 2026, full shutdown Nov 30 2026.
quote: OpenAI is deprecating the Evals platform, with evals becoming read-only for existing users on October 31, 2026, and the platform scheduled to shut down on November 30, 2026.

claim: Anthropic's Claude Console Evaluation tool supports side-by-side prompt comparison, 5-point quality grading, prompt versioning, and auto-generating or CSV-importing test cases.
quote: Quality grading: Grade response quality on a 5-point scale to track improvements in response quality per prompt.

claim: Research documents self-preference bias: LLM judges favor their own outputs (which have lower perplexity/are more familiar), with larger more capable models showing stronger self-preference; GPT-4 exhibits significant self-preference bias.
quote: LLMs may favor outputs that are more familiar to them, as indicated by lower perplexity. Additionally, larger and more capable models often show stronger self-preference.

claim: To avoid self-preference, use a judge from a different provider than the model under test; running the same eval set across multiple judges and comparing agreement surfaces bias without labeled ground truth; position and verbosity biases also affect judges (>10% accuracy shift from swapping order).
quote: Using Claude to judge Claude outputs compounds self-preference... A judge from a different provider systematically reduces this... swapping the presentation order of responses can lead to accuracy shifts exceeding 10%.

claim: A frontier judge call costs 50-500x a fine-tuned classifier per call; the cascade pattern (cheap classifier first, escalate to LLM judge on close calls) plus a deterministic floor manages cost, and teams should pick judges by kappa-per-dollar on a calibration set.
quote: A frontier judge call costs 50 to 500 times a fine-tuned classifier per call... the cascade pattern runs a cheap classifier or local heuristic first, escalates to the LLM judge only on close calls

claim: Fine-tuned compact judges (Phi-3.5 Mini, Llama-3.1-8B, Prometheus 2) win on cost/latency and robustness to bias for trained rubrics, but a notable accuracy gap remains versus frontier judges like GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
quote: Fine-tuned versions of Phi-3.5 Mini and Llama-3.1-8B consistently outperform other compact models in terms of accuracy... when benchmarked against frontier models like GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, a notable performance gap remains.

claim: promptfoo (~22,000 GitHub stars) is a CLI/library for testing prompts, agents and RAGs with declarative configs and CI/CD integration, used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
quote: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs... Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration. Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
